A daemon thread is a background thread that runs to support the main program. Its defining characteristic is:
The program does not wait for daemon threads to finish before exiting.
When all non-daemon (user) threads have completed, the runtime terminates any remaining daemon threads automatically.
Press enter or click to view image in full size

Example
Imagine an application with:

• Main thread: Processes user requests.

• Daemon thread: Periodically cleans up temporary files.
If the main thread finishes, the application exits immediately — even if the cleanup thread is still running.
Python Example
import threading
import timedef background_task():
while True:
print("Working in the background...")
time.sleep(1)
t = threading.Thread(target=background_task)
t.daemon = True # Mark as daemon
t.start()
print("Main thread is done.")
time.sleep(3)
print("Exiting program.")
Output:
Main thread is done.
Working in the background...
Working in the background...
Working in the background...
Exiting program.After "Exiting program." is printed, the daemon thread is stopped automatically.
